short: A second synthesis pass on first-pass speech (M06) and modality dropout (M03) are standard; gains are small and inconsistent, earlier systems keep lower WER, and no equal-training control exists.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06), adding a second synthesis pass that takes the first pass's speech as input with the video, and training (M03), with modality dropout. Both are standard: autoregressive decoders already feed their own synthesized frames back at inference, so the paper's claim that no earlier method used audio inputs at inference holds only for a separate audio encoder, and modality dropout is common in audio-visual recognition. The gains are small and inconsistent: on GRID unseen speakers the pre-trained base reaches 17.63% WER and its best second pass 17.70%, and earlier systems keep lower WER on three of the four WER splits, leading everywhere except GRID four speakers (3.67% against 4.07%). The strongest confound is extra training: the second pass adds an encoder and retrains the shared modules, with no equal-training control. There is no listener test and no repeated run, so the claim that synthesized audio helps is not supported.
